passage: 'Type 2 coupling is the functional relationship between two calculated variables which have one or more common component variables.' (abstract, PubMed 7212790). The abstract gives no correction; the correction used is the standard remedy of an independent measurement of the shared term.
faulty: For each patient, least-squares slope of Fick VO2 = cardiac_output * (arterial_o2_content - venous_o2_content) * 10 on DO2 = cardiac_output * arterial_o2_content * 10 across the occasions; mean over patients, compared with 0.1.
fixed: For each patient, least-squares slope of vo2_expired_gas on DO2 across the occasions; mean over patients, compared with 0.1.
estimand: Faulty: mean within-patient slope between two calculated quantities that share cardiac output. Fixed: mean within-patient slope of measured consumption on calculated delivery.
model_family: Source names none. Choice: as B3A-04 per occasion, with a patient-specific baseline and within-patient fluctuation of true cardiac output (within-patient CV about 0.25) and arterial content (about 0.08); true consumption = a_i + b*DO2 + noise (b about 0.1-0.3) in the claim-true version, b = 0 in the claim-false version; venous content from the Fick identity with the true values. Reason: repeated occasions let delivery vary within each patient while the shared term varies freely.
guard_minimum: 2 occasions per patient (a slope needs 2) and at least 2 patients with a defined slope; a patient with zero variance of delivery is not counted; guards: non-finite values, selection below the minimum, zero variance.
sizes_note: Source (abstract only) states no sizes. 40 patients x 6 occasions is a realistic supply-dependency series; the corrected check is 40 small regressions. Dependence on n: not stated.
exploited_structure: Delivery and Fick consumption both contain the same cardiac output measurement on every occasion, so their within-patient fluctuations covary through it.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the abstract gives no numbers. 0.9 is the within-patient share of the variance of log delivery due to log cardiac output for within-patient coefficients of variation of 0.25 (output) and 0.08 (arterial content): 0.0625 / (0.0625 + 0.0064); it uses cardiac output and arterial content only, which the claim-false version leaves unchanged.

notes: Role: pair (ARC81 pair 2 of 2). Earlier combos for ARC81 included shared-measured-component x regression-slope; it is repeated because a within-patient slope is the natural form of the supply-dependency question, but the data structure (patients x occasions, mean of per-unit slopes) differs from B3A-04. The correction is not documented in the abstract and is flagged as not verified in the source text.
